I just spent the better part of the day with the Amish. AMA

For the most part, yes. Everyone waved to us as we drove by, and I didn't see a single kid without a smile on their faces. There was one guy who gave us a small motor for free that he had built. However, some of the men I talked to were very offstandish. One guy really wouldn't talk to me for the most part and he got visibly angry when I said he had a nice home.
You may have offended his humility. The amish have always intrigued me. What did you find most intriguing?

One of the things I was most surprised by was how cluttered their farms were. Every yard had a swingset, clothesline, multiple piles of scrap metal, buggies, and they all had these birdfeeders. They were the top of a pole, and everyone of them was a small replica of their own house. Every house had one. Every farm also had at least one extra smaller house that, from my understanding, was where some of the children lived. Every farm we went too seemed like a small shanty town.

Source: Youth and courtship

 

Is Rumspringa still practiced there or did you observe it any? I know you spent probably less than 24 hours there, but did this topic come up at all?

No, I have no idea if Rumspringa is observed or not. I did hear about some sort of auction they hold twice a month with the whole community, they had a special name for it, but it escapes me now. But it sounds like it's sort of a large auction/swap meet where they sell goods and such. I also saw some of there stores, but it seemed like every store was closed. I don't know why they were closed on a Thursday unless there is some sort of significance about it that I didn't know. There seemed to be only be grocery stores and furniture stores.

I saw multiple school houses as well, and when I say school houses, I literally mean houses. Their schools were just houses outfitted to be schools. They all seemed to be painted white with minimal windows. They gave off a creepy vibe. The school yards also all had some ancient looking playgrounds, and one school even had a sand volleyball court. Not kidding about the volleyball court.
